input.final_summary: Reviewed only the supplied unified diff. Found two actionable concerns: one correctness risk around selecting completed programs alongside active programs, and one privacy risk from logging persistent user/program identifiers with recovery day context.

content.text:
- **High** — `src/lib/program/current-program-service.ts` — Evidence: `findFirst` now includes `{ status: { in: [ProgramStatus.ACTIVE, ProgramStatus.COMPLETED] } }` without any visible ordering or preference for `ACTIVE`. If a user has both a completed prior program and a current active program, this can select the completed one and send `/progress` or `/api/program/current` to the wrong day/status. This needs either an explicit active-first/latest ordering or a regression test for “completed old program + active current program”.

- **Medium** — `src/lib/program/current-program-service.ts`, `src/app/(app)/day/[day]/page.tsx` — Evidence: new `console.error` calls log `userId`, `programId`, `currentDay`, and `requestedDay` when content is missing. In a recovery/medical-adjacent app, persistent identifiers plus recovery-day state can become sensitive operational logs. This matters for privacy, retention, and support-log exposure; prefer redacted identifiers or request-scoped correlation IDs unless these fields are explicitly approved for logs.
